Native Attacks report source reconstruction from the configured Windows PEs.
Steam PE:6a70a6d9:02711000; classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000.
These are offline source instructions and productions, not a game observation.
Reproduce with tools/extract_fortress_attack_sources.py using the fixed Python.
The script reads both actual configured executable files through CaptionImage
and the fixed native objdump. It neither builds dictionaries nor executes DF.

Report category boundary
------------------------
Steam category function 0xeaa20..0xeab14; classic 0xea9b0..0xeaaa4.
The input is report.type, a signed int16; an unsigned >353 default returns0.
The two-level switch consists of a native354-byte remap and35-entry RVA table.
The independently decoded tab-label function maps category4,5,23 to Attacks.
All356 valid announcement enum types are retained in report-category-switch.tsv.
Attacks admits exactly22 types:
  53 AMBUSH_DEFENDER
  54 AMBUSH_RESIDENT
  56 AMBUSH_THIEF_SUPPORT_SKULKING
  57 AMBUSH_THIEF_SUPPORT_NATURE
  58 AMBUSH_THIEF_SUPPORT
  59 AMBUSH_MISCHIEVOUS
  61 AMBUSH_SNATCHER_SUPPORT
  62 AMBUSH_AMBUSHER_NATURE
  63 AMBUSH_AMBUSHER
  64 AMBUSH_INJURED
  65 AMBUSH_OTHER
  66 AMBUSH_INCAPACITATED
  90 TRIGGER_WEB
  93 MEGABEAST_ARRIVAL
  94 WEREBEAST_ARRIVAL
  95 BEAST_AMBUSH
  108 ENDGAME_EVENT_1
  109 ENDGAME_EVENT_1B
  110 ENDGAME_EVENT_2
  147 BODY_TRANSFORMATION
  150 UNDEAD_ATTACK
  277 NAMED_RESIDENT_CREATURE
Types55/60/322 are Crime despite sharing the same ambush producer owner.
Other categories within saved full owner bodies are explicitly outside this tab.

Producer boundary
-----------------
The existing complete native submission inventory nominates source owners from
the current PE identities. All nominated owners and their source helpers were
disassembled again from current image bytes. Every actual instruction is saved.
There are11 producer owners and31 Attacks submission sites in each image:
  Steam 110460 / classic1103f0: type150, four submissions
  Steam a5d230 / classica5a360: type108, one submission
  Steam a5f2d0 / classica5c400: type109, one submission
  Steam a60e50 / classica5df80: type109, two submissions
  Steam a618d0 / classica5ea00: type110, one submission
  Steam da8080 / classicda2ff0: type90, one submission
  Steam e506a0 / classice4b610: type93, one submission
  Steam e51490 / classice4c400: type94, one submission
  Steam 1353940 / classic134e8b0: type147, one submission
  Steam 13547e0 / classic134f750: type93/94/95 and277, two submissions
  Steam 13625b0 / classic135d520: remaining attack/ambush branches, seventeen submissions
The exact type alternatives at shared submissions remain in native-submission-types.tsv.
Do not infer event type from the most recent lexical MOV before a shared tail.

Arrival and beast-description fields
-----------------------------------
All four owners use the full native name/creature/profession supplier1331500.
They append " has come!", capitalize the full identity+suffix, and optionally
append two spaces plus the entire nonempty caste RAW description at+0x220.
The description's first ASCII a..z is capitalized; its internal text is retained.
The status owner13547e0 accesses that same field through144ea0(...,index0x11,true),
whose body computes caste+(index<<5), copies the whole string, and capitalizes it.
No separate generated-description grammar is introduced by this helper.
The others copy the same field inline. Empty descriptions omit the entire suffix.
Each relevant branch and every invalid-index/empty-string fallback remains saved.
There is no finite enumeration of possible world-generated identity spellings or
custom RAW descriptions; native typed fields define those complete open branches.

Finite notices and unit/creature fields
--------------------------------------
decompiled-productions.tsv records exact static sentences from native operands,
including packed SIMD loads, plus each complete native dynamic source production.
Ambush type59 has both "Intruders!  Drive them away!" and the complete caste
singular+"!  Drive it away!" (caste singular+20, then256880 fallback when empty).
Types64/65 use aa3bd0 singular creature fields after injury predicate1324490.
Type66 is "There is a {creature} hidden away here."; it is not Drive them out.
The Drive them out branch belongs to type54.
Type90 uses1330c30 full actor plus hidden-web suffix. Its "caught up in the web!"
sibling has a different enum27 and does not enter Attacks.
Type147 constructs "You have transformed into a {creature}!" for the adventure
viewpoint actor, otherwise1330c30 actor+" has transformed into a {creature}!".
The target singular is caste+20 then race+20; there is no other "have" actor branch.
Terminal endgame sources108/109/110 include every barrier/treasure/apocalypse/
ancient-horror/new-pocket/divine-retribution/underworld-scream alternative.

Resident naming, native type277
------------------------------
Steam 135c22a..135c387:
  append "The "; aa3bd0(viewpoint race global239367c,plural=true)
  append " have given a resident "; 132f980(unit,true) full creature/role field
  append " the name "; getter13e5a90(unit) -> selected language_name
  if getter nonnull and name.has_name at+72:
    a94030(language_name) -> full displayed name, assign temporary string
  append temporary; append "."; submit277
The temporary already holds the resident creature/role before the optional name
assignment. When the getter is null or has_name=false, the code leaves that prior
temporary unchanged and appends it again as the name field. The observed machine
code therefore retains a second creature/role rather than an empty name in that
fallback. Both full native branches are part of this source boundary.

Army/undead source, native type150
--------------------------------
110460 has two standalone notices for walking dead or twisted night-legion forms.
A missing invading entity produces the standalone "An army is invading!".
Otherwise its complete native string rbp+400 starts with one of six fixed base
sentences selected by parley flag and entity RAW flags. It then appends these
independently optional components, in this fixed order:
  [B]commander identity/qualities [two spaces plus commander history]
  [B]troop warning
  [B]reinforcements [optional origin site]
The [B] controls belong to this same stored report; they are not separate events.
The source grammar uses optional components rather than enumerating arbitrary
proper names and historical reports as fixed sentences.

Commander source1150dc..1153ab:
  "The army is commanded by " + b92f10 full historical-figure field
  RAW flag0x85 true: append ancient/horrible demon suffix and jump directly to'.'
  otherwise commander skill95 >=9/6/3 selects talented/seasoned/competent suffix
  warrior skill97 >0 introduces ", a " or " and " depending on commander suffix
  warrior skill >=9/6/3 selects true/skilled/middling warrior;1..2 append no noun
  append'.'
Thus native low warrior-skill1..2 can leave ", a ." or a commander+" and .".
The demon path skips both commander/warrior skill suffixes entirely.
All21 exact commander combinations, including four empty quality alternatives,
are retained in decompiled-productions.tsv rather than invented demon combinations.
The optional history supplier is actual event.virtual+d0 at115371, r9=true and
trailing bool=false, with context historical figure id at rbp+350. The producer
selects events involving that figure by virtual+88, then maximum f0*100+e8,
random among ties. It does not filter the selected event's type. The complete
history virtual formatter field therefore retains the existing133-subtype
native event dispatch in announcement-negotiation-native/returned-history-dispatch.tsv;
there is no finite expansion of every possible historical event's dynamic fields.

Troop warning1153d4..1154dd:
  "Beware their " + armor + skill + mounted + full military-creature-role + '!'
  armor >=3: heavily-armored; ==2: armored; otherwise absent
  skill >=11: elite;6..10: skilled; otherwise absent
  mounted bool independently adds mounted
  full role supplier132e0c0 invokes132cc10 RAW/enum profession and aa3bd0 creature
  with plural=true; a foreign creature can appear before the complete profession
The eighteen finite modifier combinations remain separate from their open role.

Reinforcements1154f6..115762:
  "With them "
  monster-count>0 -> "come monstrous siege engineers"
  else creature-count==1 -> "comes a "; otherwise -> "come "
  selected creature id==-1 -> append'!' and skip all origin processing
  otherwise monster-count>0 -> " and ", with "a " when creature-count==1
  append132e0c0(profession99,race) or aa3bd0(race), plural by creature-count>=2
  nonnull origin site -> " from the "+site-description+" of "+site-name
  append'!'
Consequently monster-only cannot have an origin suffix. Four reinforcement
patterns can have that suffix; five patterns can omit it.
Site-description uses10cbe10 dark/empty prefix, optional aa3770 RAW adjective,
and complete10cbe50 native site-kind; site-name is b93930 full site field.
The adjective is omitted for site kind10, absent controller, or controller0x400.
The site-kind helper includes exactly these24 distinct text operands:
  fortress; mountain halls; hillocks; pits; cave; forest retreat; hamlet; town;
  shrine; labyrinth; lair; castle; fort; monastery; tower; mysterious palace;
  mysterious dungeon; mysterious lair; vault; tomb; monument; camp;
  important location; site (unsigned/default branch).
Full helper bodies include each native site subtype/flag/count branch and table.

Saved evidence
--------------
native-owners.tsv and the per-owner .asm files retain complete producer/helper bodies.
native-literals.tsv includes full containing strings and explicit packed-load width.
native-calls.tsv retains direct and indirect call operands without guessed callees.
native-branches.tsv retains branch operations and the preceding flags instruction.
native-switches.tsv reads every decoded bounded native switch table from PE bytes.
native-submission-types.tsv retains actual submission sites and CFG type alternatives.
decompiled-productions.tsv preserves finite authored source productions and open fields.
Separate name-native-* files in this directory document the personal/name-word
suppliers. Authored/user names remain distinct from generated language WORD data.
